Yellow thunderstorm warnings have been issued across the UK, with the Met Office warning of heavy downpours and flash flooding after weeks of extreme heat.

The warnings are set to come into place later on Wednesday, and cover large swathes of northern England, Northern Ireland and parts of Scotland.

The forecaster has warned that homes and businesses could be flooded and there may be disruption to transport services and power cuts.

It follows what is likely to be the hottest summer on record, with five heatwaves leaving 71.3 per cent of the country in drought.

The yellow weather warnings are set to come into force at 12pm in Northern Ireland and last until 11.59pm on Wednesday, while parts of north-east Scotland are under the alert from 2pm until 9pm.

open image in gallery The forecaster has warned of potential flash flooding after weeks of dry weather ( Nick Potts/PA Wire )

Large parts of north of England, covering Manchester, Liverpool and Newcastle upon Tyne, have been issued a warning from 7pm on Wednesday until 10am on Thursday.

It comes as parts of the UK were hit by “heavy pulses” of rain early on Wednesday, but forecasters and officials warned downpours this week would not solve the drought overnight.

Met Office data showed up to 23mm of rain fell in parts of central southern Lancashire in the 12 hours to 6am on Wednesday, with up to 13mm recorded in parts of Northern Ireland and between 6-10mm across south-west England.

In an online forecast, Met Office meteorologist Aidan McGivern said Wednesday would be a “very showery day” across the UK, with Northern Ireland and areas in western and central Scotland seeing “frequent showers with heavy downpours, hail and thunder”.

The cooler and wetter conditions come after the UK’s fifth heatwave of the summer, during which the hottest day of the year was recorded in Kew Gardens, London, on Thursday when the temperature reached 38.1C.

open image in gallery The Environment Agency and forecasters have warned downpours this week will not solve drought overnight ( Getty )

The UK is facing increasingly severe weather extremes such as heatwaves, droughts and flooding – with a risk of surface water floods as heavy rain falls on baked dry ground – as a result of climate change, caused mostly by burning fossil fuels for power stations, vehicles, heating buildings and industry.

All of Wales, and nearly three quarters of England are in drought as a result of the hot dry conditions.

The Environment Agency and Natural Resources Wales have applied to the English and Welsh governments for a drought order for the River Severn, warning of the impact the conditions are having on the Severn’s habitats and surrounding farmers.

If granted, it would require Severn Trent Water, South Staffordshire Water, Bristol Water and Hafren Dyfrdwy, to reduce the amount they abstract from the river by 5%, which they have said will not affect water supplies.

The order would also impose a cap on the amount of water the Canal and River Trust could take for the Gloucester and Sharpness Canal and reduce releases from a reservoir at the river’s headwaters to stretch the amount of available water over a longer period to support fish and other wildlife.

The warnings come after overnight rain which saw Wisley, in Surrey, break its 62-day dry streak, the longest of any area in the UK, with 1.6mm falling in the early hours.

Pakistani authorities on Wednesday asked the Supreme Court to review or withdraw an order requiring imprisoned former Prime Minister Imran Khan to receive a medical exam at a private hospital of his choice.

The government’s legal challenge could fuel anger among his supporters over his treatment in custody. It also may deepen tensions with Khan’s opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party and his family, who have pressed for prompt access to medical care at facilities of Khan's choice and more frequent prison visits.

The petition came a day after the court ordered authorities to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital in the capital Islamabad, where he would be examined by a medical board that would include his personal physician.

The government has said Khan will be taken to government hospitals whenever he needs medical care that is not available in prison. Khan has been taken to a government hospital several times for treatment of an eye condition.

In the petition, Islamabad’s chief commissioner argued the court issued the order without giving him prior notice and said Pakistan’s constitution guarantees equal treatment.

“The Constitution abhors discrimination and favoritism,” the petition said, arguing that allowing a convicted person to receive treatment at a private hospital when his medical report did not indicate a condition requiring immediate treatment could disrupt the criminal justice system.

Implementing the order could prompt other inmates to seek similar treatment outside prison, contrary to prison rules, the petition said.

The petition described Tuesday’s order as “discriminatory” and, unless it was recalled, could “open a flood gate” of prisoners seeking similar relief that cannot be granted under existing law.

Tuesday’s order came months after Khan petitioned the court for a transfer from a high-security prison to a hospital and access to his personal physicians, family and lawyers.

Also Wednesday, Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the government had no objection to providing Khan with medical care and that he would continue receiving treatment in accordance with prison rules.

But the government was challenging the part of the Supreme Court order requiring Khan to be taken to a private hospital, Tarar said.

“There is no ambiguity” about Khan receiving medical treatment, Tarar said, adding that health issues should be kept separate from politics.

Concerns about Khan’s health intensified in late January after his family said he had lost about 85% of the vision in his right eye, an assertion disputed by the government. Authorities later said Khan had regained about 70% of his vision in the eye and that his condition was improving.

The former cricket star turned politician was removed from office in a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022 and has been imprisoned since 2023 following convictions in multiple cases.

Khan’s supporters have staged repeated rallies across the country demanding his release in recent years, some of which have turned violent.

The civil war within Reform UK has intensified after a high-profile ally of Nigel Farage vowed to challenge his suspension to test whether the party can “tolerate free speech”.

Tim Montgomerie, a commentator and senior party figure, was suspended on Tuesday after he criticised home affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf for not being a “team player”.

He has been openly critical of Mr Yusuf in recent weeks and even publicly suggested in a podcast that “Nigel has fallen out of love with Zia”.

open image in gallery Tim Montgomerie has vowed to make his suspension ‘test case’ ( BBC )

Mr Montgomerie told the BBC’s Newsnight programme that he is "going to fight" his suspension.

He said: "I think if that is the sort of censorship that the party wants to impose on me, that is not healthy.

"I'm gonna make this a test case of whether it is a party that can tolerate free speech and dissent."

He added: "I am going to fight this suspension. I want to stay in Reform. I believe that Reform's policies from immigration to crime to the ones that Robert Jenrick announced yesterday on welfare are the right ones for this country."

Earlier, in a statement on his suspension, he also claimed that Mr Farage had not known about it before it happened.

open image in gallery The civil war within Nigel Farage’s party has burst into the open ( Matthew Chattle/Shutterstock )

Last week Reform’s leader hit out at Mr Yusuf for calling a former Tory defence secretary, and soldier, Ben Wallace a “traitor”.

Speaking on The Spectator’s Coffee House Shots podcast earlier this week, Mr Montgomerie said of Mr Yusuf: “It was unprecedented for Farage to criticise him last week, but did he take down the tweet that Nigel criticised? No. He wouldn’t. He’s loyal to Nigel as he has to be if he wants to succeed him, but in terms of being able to really play as a team player...”

“He has consistently freelanced on Twitter, on, for example, accepting Conservative candidates, Suella Braverman and Robert Jenrick, even though he knew they were being wooed. But it was his way of trying to undermine that policy.”

Reform said its general secretary and chair “have had months of complaints regarding Tim’s behaviour and conduct. They saw fit to take action and protect the party”.

A senior Reform source also said the party would “never engage in the Tory briefing wars and toxicity that goes with them - the correct course of action has been taken. Disagreements should happen behind closed doors, not in the eye of the national media.”

The row within Reform has overshadowed what should be a good week for the party, after Mr Farage was returned to Parliament on Friday with victory in the Clacton by-election.

News.title: Unemployment rate fails to fall for Burnham
News.content:
An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics. Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

While the three-month figure was flat, monthly data showed a sharp increase at the end of the period. Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

That marked the highest reading since October 2020 and the biggest monthly jump in 13 years.

Julian Jessop, at the Institute of Economic Affairs, described the latest jobs figures as “dire”.

He said: “The unemployment rate remains stubbornly high, with a big jump in the single month figure for June.”

It came as private sector wage growth slumped to a six-year low of just 2.8pc. That stands in contrast to a 6.1pc pay increase for the average public sector worker in the same period.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.

Ben Harrison, director of the Work Foundation at Lancaster University, warned that the UK was “trapped in a deepening jobs drought”.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “Stagnant, or even negative, real wage growth in the second half of this year will intensify the pressure on Burnham and Healey to come up with a package to support the cost of living.

“However, doing anything substantial without breaching either the fiscal rules or the manifesto commitments looks increasingly difficult given the deterioration in headroom and commitments to spend big on everything from defence to social care.”

News.title: Top British scientist steps down from WHO
News.content:
One of Britain’s best-known scientists has resigned as assistant director-general of the World Health Organization.

Sir Jeremy Farrar became a household name during the pandemic when he served on the UK’s Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies (Sage).

Sources inside the WHO and the broader scientific community told The Telegraph he resigned his position on Monday.

While it is not clear what prompted his resignation, colleagues told The Telegraph he had been unhappy within the organisation for some time. One speculated that he had become increasingly frustrated with its internal politics and bureaucracy.

Sir Jeremy, 64, who was also a former director of the Wellcome Trust, could not immediately be reached for comment.

The surprise move comes at a difficult time for the WHO, which is undergoing a major restructuring after suffering cuts and a massive funding shortfall following the United States’s withdrawal from it in January. It is also fighting a major outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO’s Director-General, announced Dr Farrar’s decision in an email to all staff on Tuesday morning, saying that the British scientist will “retire” from the WHO, effective September 30.

In the email, seen by The Telegraph, Dr Tedros said: “Dr Farrar has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to science and public health at the highest levels, and we are grateful that he chose to bring his experience, energy and conviction to WHO.

“On behalf of the entire organisation, I extend my sincere thanks to Dr Farrar... [and wish] him every success in his next chapter and a well-deserved retirement.”

He added that Dr Bruce Aylward will take over as the new Assistant Director-General for Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Care.

News.title: Rabies deaths are rising. What is going wrong?
News.content:
In a packed intensive care ward in Dhaka, three-year-old Abdul lay paralysed, his tiny body contorted by a rabies infection that had reached his brain.

His mother, Sheuli Akter, 38, sat at his side massaging his legs in the hope that this might loosen his muscles, but it was having no effect. Even his hands and feet were seized up by cramps.

Abdul had been in the hospital for a month but doctors said he was unlikely to live much longer. The infection, they said, had progressed to degenerative encephalitis; the virus had got to his brain.

Abdul was shaking, gripped by fever. His breathing was rapid and panicked, punctuated occasionally by groans of pain.

On his chin was the telltale scar of a dog bite, the source of the infection.

“He was playing outside with the other children,” said Sheuli. “The dog, which was one of those always waiting around outside, suddenly attacked him. They said it went for him because he was the smallest.”

News.title: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
News.content:
Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

“It would be triple or quadruple our wage bill!

“Jose’s always there. Between us now, I did message him the other day about another player, not a Real Madrid player – but a player that he worked with previously and he’s always on call.

“It takes him a couple of days sometimes. I know he’s a busy man.

But what is clear is that, Lampard and Mourinho have maintained a close bond despite their relationship becoming more complicated over the years.

Mourinho was Lampard’s manager during his hugely successful first spell at Chelsea, with the midfielder becoming one of the most important players in the club’s history.



Lampard recalled one famous conversation with Mourinho in the shower shortly after the Portuguese’s arrival at Stamford Bridge in 2004.

The former England star said Mourinho told him he was already the best player in the world, but needed to win trophies to be recognised as such.

He later admitted Mourinho’s influence on his own managerial career remains significant.



Lampard said: “We’ve got that connection forever now, the Chelsea boys, Jose and that little group that you saw in the documentary, and those sort of bonds do stay forever.”

And while Lampard insists he has developed his own style as a manager, he admitted he has taken plenty from Mourinho.

Sports.content:
Champions League winner looks unrecognisable as he plays for 9th division side aged 30

This Champions League winner stunned with a vastly different look than the footballing public were used to

View 4 Images Niklas Sule made a stunning return to football (Image: Julian Finney)

Former Bayern Munich defender Niklas Sule has undergone a dramatic transformation just months after retiring from professional football. Sule, 30, starred for the Bundesliga giants from 2017 to 2022 while winning 14 major honours, including five league titles and the Champions League as part of their historic treble in 2020.

‌



The centre-back joined Borussia Dortmund after five years in Bavaria and reached a second European final in 2024, but lost 2-0 to Real Madrid. Sule opted to end his glittering career at the end of the 2025/26 campaign due to persistent knee injuries.

‌



He had torn his ACL twice before and almost did it a third time against former club Hoffenheim in the final weeks of last season. The scare caused him to call it quits, but Sule didn't stay away from the football pitch for long.

‌



Less than three months after his decision, the ex-Germany international returned to play for ninth-tier German side SV Tiefenbach. He cut a drastically different look than when he played in his last professional match against boyhood club Eintracht Frankfurt in May earlier this year.

Sports.title: Jamal Musiala's condition explained after 'neurological dysfunction' causes second collapse
Sports.content:
Jamal Musiala's condition explained after 'neurological dysfunction' causes second collapse

Jamal Musiala revealed that he's suffering from a condition after collapsing for the second time in four days during Bayern Munich's pre-season friendly against Heidenheim on Tuesday

View 3 Images Jamal Musiala has opened up on his diagnosis (Image: EyesWideOpen/Getty Images)

Bayern Munich star Jamal Musiala has revealed that a 'neurological dysfunction' caused him to collapse in their last two matches. Musiala, 23, fell to the floor for the second time in four days when German giants Bayern faced Heidenheim in a pre-season friendly.

‌



Like in the clash with RB Leipzig on Saturday, multiple team-mates spotted him falling and rushed to his aid, with England captain Harry Kane earning special praise for his reaction. After the match, Musiala posted a detailed description on Instagram and confirmed that he's suffering from ' treatable absence seizures'.

‌



"I know these might look scary at first glance - but right now, they're just part of my daily life," the midfielder explained. "I am receiving the best possible medical care and am very optimistic."

‌



So what exactly is Musiala's condition?

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Absence seizures cause a person to suffer from a sudden, brief lapse in awareness. The person often stares blankly for a few seconds, unlike someone's body jerking during a myoclonic seizure.

According to both NHS and NICE guidelines, absence seizures are highly treatable through specific anti-seizure medications managed by a specialist. Professor Christoph Kleinschnitz - head of neurology at the University Hospital Essen, Germany - spoke to Bild about the condition following Musiala's collapses.

"From a neurological perspective, this could potentially be an epileptic seizure," Kleinschnitz said. "It could be a form of absence epilepsy, as symptoms such as brief periods of unresponsiveness are consistent with it.

‌



"However, we would need to know all the findings from the neurological examinations to make that assessment. It is highly treatable, but would require long-term therapy. Musiala can continue playing football."

View 3 Images Jamal Musiala's condition is 'highly treatable' (Image: EyesWideOpen/Getty Images)

Musiala's post on Instagram shed further light on the condition, saying that 'there is no additional health risk'. "First things first - I'm doing fine," the Germany international began.

‌



"I am particularly grateful for your messages and your support! I understand that many of you are worried. I want to put your minds at ease today and explain a few things: I have been diagnosed with temporary, brief, but well-treatable absences (absence seizures) caused by a neurological dysfunction.

"These can lead to the kind of moments that happened recently, such as against Leipzig or now in Heidenheim. I know these might look scary at first glance - but right now, they're just part of my daily life.

"I am receiving the best possible medical care and am very optimistic. FC Bayern and my personal circle are always by my side, supporting me on this journey.

‌



View 3 Images Jamal Musiala has collapsed in Bayern Munich's last two games (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

"Most importantly, there is no additional health risk beyond this. In close consultation and regular communication with experts, it was my personal wish to face this challenge and - with clearance from neurological specialists - to keep focusing on what helps my recovery most: simply living my everyday life and continuing to pursue my passion for playing football.

"I have taken full responsibility for this decision. Overall, I feel very good about it and am on the right track. What helps me most on this path is to keep chasing victories and titles alongside my team and with your fantastic support.

‌



"I hope this helps you understand my situation better. At the same time, I kindly ask for your understanding that I wish to keep this matter private, within the circle of my closest confidants, the club, and the medical experts."

Bayern's next fixture is a clash with Borussia Dortmund in the German Super Cup on Saturday. They'll then start their Bundesliga title defence at home to Stuttgart on Friday.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford 'seriously impressing' club chiefs with actions towards two Man Utd stars
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford 'seriously impressing' club chiefs with actions towards two Man Utd stars

Marcus Rashford's future has been constantly unpacked this summer, but things may now be changing for the Manchester United forward

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford has been playing a role in JJ Gabriel's development (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford has been working closely with Manchester United 15-year-old prodigy JJ Gabriel and prospect Shea Lacey in a mentor capacity. Rashford, 28, has looked set for an Old Trafford exit this summer, but his work with the youngsters is the latest sign he will remain with his boyhood club.

‌



He has not played a Premier League match for United since December 2024, having been sent out on loan to Aston Villa and Barcelona. After the latter decided not to sign him permanently for £26million, Rashford now looks set to stay, despite both parties seemingly wanting a transfer earlier this summer.

‌



Michael Carrick has reintegrated him into the squad and even deployed him in United's recent pre-season loss to AC Milan. While Rashford has not got the dream move to Barcelona he craved, he has not been sulking.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Instead, the United academy graduate has been working closely with the Reds' graduates of 2026, which include prodigy Gabriel and bright star Lacey. According to the Daily Mail, his efforts in this regard have "seriously impressed" those in charge at the club.

Furthermore, it is believed that the likelihood of Rashford remaining with the Red Devils is growing with each passing day. Carrick has already held extensive discussions with the England international, who was given a tour of United's brand new £50m training facility.

‌



Rashford has also been reunited with close friend Youri Tielemans, with whom he struck up a bond during his stint at Aston Villa. Former United skipper Harry Maguire has also thrown his weight behind Rashford staying at the club beyond the summer transfer window.

View 3 Images Rashford has been lending his experience to United's young stars (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

He recently said: "He's a huge threat to have in your team, if he's going to stay with us. Obviously the transfer window is still open, but we hope as players that he stays and he's a big asset to have.

‌



"I've played with Marcus for numerous years and I know that from playing against him, and playing with him in training, he is going to help us."

Last season, Rashford's standout displays earned him a spot in Thomas Tuchel's England squad for the recent World Cup. During his time at the Camp Nou, he racked up an impressive 14 goals and 14 assists across 49 appearances.

View 3 Images Rashford has been all smiles since he started training with United again (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



His efforts played a pivotal role in clinching La Liga, marking the first league title of his footballing career. It is claimed that the prospect of a permanent move to Barcelona this summer remains very much alive.

TEAMtalk recently reported Barcelona's hierarchy remain in contact with Rashford's representatives, despite having already brought in Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon this summer. United kick off their Premier League campaign this Saturday with a trip to newly promoted Hull City.

Sports.content:
BBC 'seal deal' to show 38 live matches from top European league on free-to-air TV

BBC are set to show one match a week on free-to-air television from one of Europe's top leagues after expanding its coverage for the new season

View 2 Images Serie A is set to appear on BBC (Image: Andrea Staccioli/Insidefoto/LightRocket via Getty Images)

BBC will show Serie A matches this season after agreeing a deal to televise 38 matches from this weekend. BBC Scotland are set to lead the coverage but games are also set to be shown on iPlayer as the broadcast expands.

‌



One match from each gameweek will be shown across the season, and will be shared between BBC Scotland and BBC Alba. Last season, the latter showed eight games from the Italian top flight.

‌



The coverage is described as a network offering, with BBC Scotland running production. Last year, the broadcaster harked back to Channel 4's Football Italia and built upon the nostalgia by utilising presenter James Richardson for a guest appearance ahead of Napoli's clash with Bologna.

‌



The rights will be shared with TNT Sports and DAZN, with BBC ALBA covering games in a mix of Gaelic and English. A source told the Scotsman that the decision to invest in coverage was a 'no-brainer'.

“The opportunity to continue and expand our coverage across BBC iPlayer for the coming season was a no-brainer," they said. "We are bringing live European football to a free-to-air audience. Arguably, Serie A remains the most glamorous league in the world, and with even more British players this season. We hope the coverage goes down well.”

Interest in Serie A has only increased in Scotland in recent years, with plenty of representation in the division. Scott McTominay's emergence as a star in the league, as Napoli won the title in 2024/25, captured the imagination.

‌



The former Manchester United midfielder is joined by Billy Gilmour in Campania as they look to reclaim their title from Inter Milan after falling short last term.

It will be Josh Doig and Kieron Bowie who are on television first. The Sassuolo duo will face off against Atalanta in the first match of the deal on Sunday, with the latter returning to the division on loan after being relegated with Verona in 2025/26.

Che Adams still represents Torino, while Lennon Miller will line up for Udinese. Despite transfer speculation, Lewis Ferguson is expected to continue to feature for Bologna for the time being.

Sports.title: Everton chief drops fresh hint over Jack Grealish return - ‘We’ve remained in contact’
Sports.content:
Everton chief drops fresh hint over Jack Grealish return - ‘We’ve remained in contact’

Jack Grealish spent last season on loan with Everton from Manchester City albeit saw his spell on Merseyside cruelly cut short by injury and his future still remains up in the air

View 2 Images Jack Grealish has now returned to Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

Jack Grealish remains ‘in contact’ with Everton as he attempts to clarify his Manchester City future. The England international spent last season on loan with the Toffees in an attempt to relaunch his career.

‌



Grealish, 30, enjoyed a bright start to life on Merseyside, scoring twice and providing six assists in 22 appearances before seeing his loan spell cruelly cut short by a long-term injury.

‌



He opted to stay with Everton throughout his recovery and the club’s CEO Angus Kinnear has since revealed that conversations remain ongoing with the winger, albeit stopped short of confirming whether he would be rejoining the club.

‌



"Jack [Grealish] is a player we've remained in contact with," Kinnear told BBC Radio Merseyside. "It was no secret that he decided to have his rehabilitation done here for the remainder of last season when he didn't have to do that.

"He's a player who's fallen in love with the right shade of blue but ultimately he's a Manchester City player at the moment and we need to respect that.

‌



"The most important thing is he's back. He had a very serious injury, he's worked really hard to get back from that."

Grealish has already made one appearance for Man City this season, having been introduced at the break of the Community Shield defeat to Arsenal.

Speaking about the winger, new City boss Enzo Maresca said: "Jack was inside when we were 2-0 down so the game already became complicated after that, but overall I think Jack was good.

‌



“The ones that are still here and want to work every day and if they deserve they're going to get minutes. At the moment the transfer window is open and we will see what happens."

View 2 Images Grealish enjoyed a productive spell at Everton before injury (Image: Getty Images)

Grealish joined City from boyhood club Aston Villa back in 2021 for £100m and has gone on to make 158 appearances, albeit has scored just 17 times. He has however helped the club to three Premier League titles, the Champions League and the FA Cup. Grealish’s current deal with City is set to run until next summer.

‌



The 39-time England international caused a bit of a stir over recent days, having been spotted at Cardiff City’s Championship opener against Wrexham, albeit there is no suggestion that he could sign for either of the two sides.

He was however asked by one of the home supporters whether his appearance was a permanent deal or a loan, with Grealish jokingly replying that he didn’t know yet.

He will hope to be in contention this weekend as Man City kick off their Premier League season against Bournemouth at the Etihad Stadium.

Sports.content:
Rodri fires dig at Arsenal in emotional Man City farewell as Barcelona move confirmed

Rodri has joined Barcelona on a four-year contract in a deal worth £65million, and the midfielder has managed to take a swipe at Arsenal while saying goodbye to Manchester City

Rodri completes Barcelona switch from Manchester City

Rodri fired a parting shot at Arsenal in his emotional goodbye letter to Manchester City. The 30-year-old has joined Barcelona for £65million, signing a four-year contract with the La Liga giants.

‌



His move was confirmed on Tuesday, having snubbed interest from Real Madrid to sign for Barca and return to Spain after seven trophy-laden seasons at the Etihad. Rodri was instrumental in City's success, particularly during Premier League title races in which they went-to-head with Arsenal.

‌



Under Pep Guardiola, City twice pipped the Gunners to the title before Mikel Arteta's side finally got their hands on the trophy in May. But Rodri didn't mention any of those battles, instead bringing up his stoppage-time goal that gave City a controversial 2-1 victory at the Emirates in 2022.

‌



View 2 Images Rodri has been unveiled at Barcelona (Image: Eric Alonso/Getty Images)

The midfielder said: "Many incredible moments come to my mind. My first trophy at City, in my first game. The last minute winners, like Arsenal away. Scoring in the (Aston) Villa game to reach the Premier League, when it looked so tough.

"Scoring the goal to win the Champions League that we all wanted so much. The incredible reception you gave me after the Ballon d'Or.

"You cannot imagine how proud I am to be the first player to win this award in a sky blue shirt. Making history, with the Treble, with Four in a Row. We saw things they'll never see."

‌



Rodri is no stranger to making a dig towards Arsenal. After City's title win in 2024, he suggested that the Gunners had a 'mentality' problem.

Although Rodri will no longer be fighting with Arsenal domestically, he could face them in the Champions League with Barcelona. His arrival puts Hansi Flick and Co. among the favourites to win the competition, having done so with City in 2023 as part of their famous treble.

"It was a tough decision. Firstly because I was leaving City, who gave me everything. I was really happy there and will always be grateful. I appreciate how they facilitated my exit.

"Barcelona has always been a reference for me because of the values and the playing style here. It's true I had another offer, but Barca was the first option and I told the board here that."

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola's dream Curtis Jones replacement as Liverpool sign £78m star everyone wants
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola's dream Curtis Jones replacement as Liverpool sign £78m star everyone wants

Curtis Jones's future is up in the air – and that could represent an opportunity for Liverpool

View 2 Images Curtis Jones could be on the way out the door (Image: Nikki Dyer/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

One option stands out above all the rest if Liverpool need to replace Curtis Jones this summer. Jones has been the subject of major transfer interest and could still leave before the window slams shut.

‌



Iraola previously admitted he would like to keep the midfielder at Liverpool for the upcoming season. Speaking in July, the Reds boss dubbed the midfielder a "great player" and urged him to remain at Anfield.

‌



Iraola said: "It’s very important that he’s Scouse, that he’s from here. I also like the personality. From the outside at least he looks like a player with good character and I hope we can keep him, not only for this year but for more time."

‌



However, those words arguably bely the current situation that Jones finds himself in. Inter Milan have been after Jones since January and have seen two bids knocked back for the 25-year-old.

Milos Kerkez gives Andoni Iraola verdict as Arne Slot's issues at Liverpool become clearer READ MORE :

The second of those was worth £21.7million back in June, while further contact was made last month over a potential £30million deal. However, that still falls short of Liverpool's valuation of £35m.

Ultimately the two clubs are not poles apart over a valuation for a player who will leave Anfield for free next summer – if he does not move now or agree a new deal with the Reds. Should he depart, that would leave Iraola a little short in midfield, both in more general terms and when it comes to proven experience.

‌



In an ideal scenario, a Jones exit would be followed by a swift replacement – and one of a higher calibre. Iraola's dream replacement on that basis would potentially be Crystal Palace's Adam Wharton; a player who has long been linked with a move to Liverpool.

The 22-year-old is in high demand, with reported interest in him also coming from the likes of Real Madrid, Manchester United and Chelsea.

Palace are desperate to keep hold of the midfielder and have slapped a £78m price tag on his head. His acquisition would act as the perfect defensive reinforcement for Iraola, with his impressive rate of interceptions and his short-passing game marking him out as a quality addition.

Not only that but Liverpool would also be getting a player yet to hit the peak of his powers. Wharton has excelled both at home and in Europe at the age of 22. There can be no doubt that there is still plenty more to come from the former Blackburn Rovers man.

To that end he would fit seamlessly into a team that looks to have progression in its DNA. Hugo Ekitike is still only 24, Jeremy Jacquet is 21, Giovanni Leoni is 19, Florian Wirtz and Victor Munoz are both 23, while Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumhoa are also in their teens. All of them would expect to be in and around the Liverpool first-team this season.

Adding Wharton to the line-up would also allow Ryan Gravenberch to play further forward and provide assistance to Dominik Szoboszlai in attacking areas.

Of course, the England international wouldn't come cheap – and any move would likely depend on Jones's own future. But as dream replacements go, Wharton would be right up there.

Sports.title: Man Utd close to full agreement with Brighton for Baleba
Sports.content:
Manchester United are close to a full agreement with Brighton to sign Carlos Baleba.

The club already have a five-year contract ready for him to sign when the deal is formally concluded. The final fee and structure are not yet fully agreed, but the deal is expected to be worth in excess of £60m.

The 22-year-old is understood to be preparing to travel to Manchester, where medical plans will also be scheduled swiftly once the deal is completed.

Sky Sports News has been reporting on United's interest in Baleba since last autumn and broke the news that they enquired about signing him during the January transfer window.

Baleba is currently recovering from an ankle ligament injury he picked up during pre-season, but it's not expected to keep him out for an extended period.

He has remained one of United's top targets this summer and is set to become their third addition in midfield after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Baleba joined Brighton from Lille in 2023 and has made 112 appearances for the club. He featured 35 times last season and was absent for a spell while representing Cameroon at the Africa Cup of Nations.

Is Baleba a major gamble or a game-changer for Man Utd?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Dan Khan and Tim Sherwood react to the breaking news that Manchester United are close to an agreement for the signing of Brighton's Carlos Baleba

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

A year ago, Carlos Baleba appeared to have the world at his feet.

A breakout season at Brighton had established the then-21-year-old as one of the Premier League's most coveted young midfielders, with a move to one of Europe's elite clubs seemingly inevitable. Manchester United were among those interested, having identified Baleba as a potential transformative presence in midfield.

But Brighton's reported £100m-plus valuation proved a stumbling block. The move never materialised and Baleba stayed at the Amex.

His form subsequently dipped dramatically. His numbers fell and, at times, he looked a shadow of the midfielder who had generated so much excitement the previous season.

That makes United's interest a gamble. But, stylistically, there are few midfielders better suited to what they need.

Image: Baleba was among the league's leading defensive midfielders during the 2024/25 season - can he revive that form?

United require greater authority in the middle of the pitch and, crucially, someone capable of winning the ball back in deeper areas. Baleba brings exactly that. His athleticism, aggression and ability to carry the ball through midfield would add a level of dynamism and steel that is currently missing.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been astute additions, but Baleba offers something different: specialist defensive power coupled with the athleticism to drive United up the pitch.

His age is another major factor. Baleba is still only 22 and, despite his inconsistent season, there remains a belief around him that he can develop into one of the world's best midfielders.

That ambition is reflected in his influences. Baleba has spoken of his admiration for Paul Pogba, Yaya Toure and Andres Iniesta, while Neymar and Ronaldinho were among his favourite players to watch. There is a desire for self-expression in his game that goes beyond the physical qualities that made so highly rated.

There is risk attached to signing him. United would be betting on the player Baleba can become rather than simply the one he has been over the past 12 months.

But if United want to find a midfielder capable of growing into one of the best in his position, this is exactly the sort of gamble they should be willing to take.

Sports.title: Brook returns to top of Test batting rankings
Sports.content:
England batter Harry Brook has returned to the top of the ICC men's Test batting rankings, with Australia's Travis Head dropping down after a couple of low scores in their shock Test defeat to Bangladesh.

It is Brook's fourth stint at No 1, coming as England's new era under returning captain Joe Root gets under way with the first Test of the three-match series against Pakistan at Headingley - live on Sky Sports.

Brook first claimed top spot in December 2024.

Image: Steve Smith has moved up to third after being one of Australia's rare bright spots during their Test defeat to Bangladesh at Darwin

Joe Root and Steve Smith have also overtaken Head in the rankings, with Smith scoring 71 and 44 in that Test defeat to Bangladesh in Darwin to move into third position.

Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto has reached a career-best 20th position, with his knock of 84 in his only innings lifting him nine places and above the likes of India all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja and compatriot Litton Das.

Cameron Green's second-innings century has seen him to advance five positions to 30th.

'Hugely supportive' Brook to remain vice-captain

Brook, despite serving as vice-captain, was overlooked for the England Test captaincy in favour of Root following Ben Stokes' international retirement during the final match of the series defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast Nasser Hussain, believes Harry Brook is a 'very good captain' but need the 'mature Harry to come out' after his England Test captaincy snub.

Root confirmed Brook will continue in the role for the Pakistan series and insisted the pair's bond remains strong.

"Our relationship is exactly as it has been for a long time," Root said on Tuesday. "Me and Harry are very good friends and get along well away from cricket, and clearly get the best out of each other when playing together.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root says that he feels as ready as any other England captain to have gone before ahead of his second tenure as England Test cricket captain.

"He's been hugely supportive. I fully feel like he's got my back, as the rest of the guys do. He's going to be invaluable.

"He's done some brilliant things already within the white-ball space. He's a brilliant leader within the group and the fact he's not captain, that shouldn't be taken away from him."

Sports.title: Rangers sign Nedeljkovic from Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Rangers have signed right-back Kosta Nedeljkovic from Aston Villa.

The 20-year-old has moved to Ibrox on a season-long loan, with a £4m obligation to buy included in the deal, which will be triggered based on the number of games he plays.

Sky Sports News understands Rangers saw off competition from other clubs to sign Nedeljkovic after he held talks with manager Derek McInnes and his Serbia team-mate Vanja Dragojevic, who moved to the club earlier this summer.

Image: Summer signing Vanja Dragojevic played a key role in helping seal Nedeljkovic's move to Ibrox

Nedeljkovic arrived at Villa Park in January 2024 from Red Star Belgrade but made 10 appearances in that time, having also spent a season and a half on loan at RB Leipzig.

Rangers have now made 11 summer signings, with more expected over the coming weeks of the transfer window.

It is understood Ibrox chiefs are searching for a new striker and winger before the September 3 deadline in Scotland, with Portland Timbers' Kevin Kelsy and Brighton's Amario Cozier-Duberry among those of interest to Rangers.

Image: Derek McInnes is expected to further add to his squad over the coming weeks

Speaking after joining Rangers, Nedeljković said: "I am very excited, Rangers is such a big club, a big family and I am excited to join and help the team have success together.

"For me, it was an easy decision after meeting with the coach, I only wanted Rangers. It is a big opportunity and a big responsibility. I always try to be positive and work hard so I am ready to help the team."

Manager McInnes added: "Kosta is a talented young player who we are really pleased to bring to the club.

"He has already gained some valuable experience at a high level in England and Germany, as well as representing Serbia internationally. Kosta is an athletic and energetic full-back who is keen to get forward, but he also has a real desire to defend and compete and he will further strengthen a key area for us.

"I look forward to welcoming Kosta to Rangers, and working with him moving forward."
