Sports.title: Manchester United close in on Carlos Baleba as Red Devils eye cut-price deal just one year after £115m price tag
Sports.content:
Manchester United close in on Carlos Baleba as Red Devils eye cut-price deal just one year after £115m price tag

Manchester United are in advanced talks to sign Carlos Baleba from Brighton, talkSPORT understands.

The Red Devils are confident of agreeing a deal for less than £75million.



2 The Cameroon international has been with Brighton since August 2023 Credit: Getty

Baleba has already agreed personal terms wit the Red Devils.

Has Manchester United previously gone after Carlos Baleba?

The 22-year-old was heavily courted by the Red Devils last season but a deal never came to fruition as Brighton took a hard line stance on keeping the midfielder at the club, valuing him at around £115million.

Once it became clear he would not move to Old Trafford, Baleba endured a dip in performances.

The Cameroon international was taken off at half-time in three of Brighton's opening seven Premier League fixtures last term.



In response to Baleba's worrying displays, Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler conceded there was a chance the 22-year-old had been affected by United's interest.

"For sure, when a young boy reads there is interest from Manchester United with a big, big offer, it might affect him deep, deep down,” Hurzeler said.



“That’s also part of the development to understand that when you play well, there comes a big offer, there comes a big club who wants to have him.

“But then to keep pushing, to be humble, stay here in Brighton, and try to make the next step with the team and that’s something we have to keep on working with him.



“I can’t give you a clear answer if it’s really affected him or not. But for sure, he’s a young boy and we need to understand he’s not a machine that if you click on then he always runs and off then he stops.

“We need to understand his feelings, his emotions, where he comes from, and that’s our responsibility."

2 Carrick is eyeing Baleba as another option to strengthen United's midfield Credit: Getty

Which other clubs are interested in Carlos Baleba?

Although United may be the front-runners for Baleba, they are not alone in the race for his signature.



talkSPORT understands Baleba is on Newcastle's radar as an option to replace Bruno Guimaraes.

The Magpies have a serious void in the heart of their midfield following Guimaraes' move to Arsenal.

However, Baleba is far from Newcastle's only midfield target, with Manchester City's Nico Gonzalez also on the shortlist.

Which players have Manchester United signed this summer?

The potential addition of Baleba continues United's midfield overhaul this summer.



Youri Tielemans joined from Aston Villa after the Red Devils triggered his £35m release clause while Andrey Santos arrived from Chelsea for £50m.

United also have Kobbie Mainoo in their midfield ranks, with the England international penning a new deal until 2031 in April.

Sports.title: Ethan Nwaneri ‘could be a massive hit’ if he moves to surprise Europa League club
Sports.content:
Ethan Nwaneri ‘could be a massive hit’ if he moves to surprise Europa League club

Ethan Nwaneri could light up the Bundesliga with a move to Bayer Leverkusen as the race to sign him hots up.

talkSPORT revealed last weekend that the Arsenal star is expected to leave the Gunners before the end of the transfer window.

5 Bayer Leverkusen have been named as an ideal landing spot for Nwaneri Credit: Getty

Nwaneri was left out by Mikel Arteta in his 20-man squad for the 3-0 Community Shield win against Manchester City on Sunday.

The club's academy graduate made just four starts across 12 appearances for Arsenal in the first half of last season after falling out of favour.

Just 12 months earlier, Nwaneri was drawing comparisons to England star Jude Bellingham and Spain's talisman, Lamine Yamal.

talkSPORT's Adrian Durham even went so far as to say it is a 'sackable offence' for Thomas Tuchel not to pick the teenager in his first England squad in March 2025.

The 19-year-old became the youngest player in Premier League history upon making his first-team debut against Brentford in 2022 aged 15 years and 181 days.

It was hoped that a loan move to Marseille in January to work under Roberto De Zerbi would reignite his development.

Ethan Nwaneri at Marseille

Nwaneri duly scored just 13 minutes into his debut, yet he found himself out of the team when De Zerbi - now the Tottenham boss - left the club.

Arsenal's No.22 was then an unused sub in five of Marseille's final six Ligue 1 games last season as the loan spell came to a sorry conclusion.

European football expert Andy Brassell explained to talkSPORT.com: "I can understand all the reasoning for Arteta sending him out to Marseille last season. And De Zerbi spent the first half of last season talking about how he wanted his number 10 to build around.

5 Nwaneri made just four appearances under De Zerbi Credit: Getty

"Clearly Arsenal loaned him to Marseille with the understanding that it was for De Zerbi. And De Zerbi would be the guy to develop him and have new and fresh ideas, and work with him and bring him on and give him responsibility as the central part in the team.

"Of course, he could play on the right-hand side cutting in.

"He did a little bit play on the right-hand side cutting in, at least until De Zerbi went. But really the idea was for Mason Greenwood to keep his spot there and Nwaneri to be the number 10.

"And then there were a few little teething problems. And that became a massive problem once De Zerbi went.

"Of course, maybe this is easy to say in retrospect, but I said it at the time actually. If you're pitching the wagon to De Zerbi a little bit too much when it's clear that his position was a little bit unstable.

"There was a lot going on emotionally at Marseille. He could leave at any point. And that kind of left Nwaneri in a really difficult position."

5 Nwaneri scored twice and registered one assist in nine Ligue 1 appearances Credit: Getty

Nwaneri transfer latest

Nwaneri would have hoped to hit the ground running back at pre-season with Arsenal after training with the England squad in the United States ahead of the World Cup.

However, his future now looks unclear following his absence on Sunday, with the German league touted as a potential landing spot.

Brassell added: "Depending on what sort of position you're going to put him in, I think the Bundesliga would be a good spot for him.

"Before Borussia Dortmund made their last couple of signings, notably that of [Konstantinos] Karetsas, I would have seen him being a really good fit for Dortmund. But now they've gone out there, and they've signed Karetsas.

"Giannis Konstantelias is coming as well from PAOK. They're not going to have the spot for him."

5 Nwaneri registered six Premier League goal involvements in 2024/25 compared to zero last season

Nwaneri to Leverkusen?

"I wonder if Leverkusen could be a good spot for him because they're looking for a right-sided, left-footed player," he continued.

"Now, again, that's not Nwaneri as a number 10, but I think just because we've had it in our heads for a couple of years that he should be the ultimate or eventual [Martin] Odegaard replacement; It doesn't mean that's all he can do.

"And I think him acting as a sort of wide playmaker and especially one who can come inside and score goals; I think that would be really good."

Leverkusen already have a No.10 in their squad, which is where Nwaneri views his best position, having handed Florian Wirtz's shirt number to USA international Malik Tillman last season.

Yet Carles Martínez Novell's men, who will be playing in the Europa League this season, have a pre-existing relationship with Arteta's Arsenal, having sanctioned the £34.5m exit of Piero Hincapie.

The Gunners were also touted to have held discussions over a potential deal for Nwaneri's fellow Englishman, Jarell Quansah.

5 Quansah was named in England's World Cup squad after featuring 43 times for Leverkusen last term Credit: Getty

"Now, look, Leverkusen have got a lot of players in their squad, a lot of good players in their squad, so you'd have to battle for space," Brassell told talkSPORT. "There's no doubt about that. But they are looking for a player in that exact spot [on the right].

"They're hoping to do a deal to bring Moussa Diaby back. Of course, he's in Saudi at the moment - Because he's in Saudi, he's waiting for a significant payoff before he leaves. And his current club would like to whack that onto the fee for Leverkusen, which they're obviously not that happy with.

"But I feel that Nwaneri could be a massive hit in the Bundesliga. Stuttgart, again, I think would be a good destination for him.

"Again, financially a little bit more difficult to do, I think. And unless there's a move out of Stuttgart, maybe he doesn't go straight into the XI there. So that's a question mark.

"Maybe it needs to be a post-Jamie Leweling thing. But I think it'd be great under the coaching of Sebastian Hoeneß.

"Leverkusen seems like a really interesting spot for me. And maybe that's something that could open up."

Sports.title: Harry Kane praised for quick thinking immediately after Jamal Musiala collapsed again
Sports.content:
Harry Kane has been hailed by fans after being the first player to notice Bayern Munich teammate Jamal Musiala had fainted again.

Both players were introduced in the 61st minute during the Bavarian outfit's final pre-season clash against Bundesliga 2 side Heidenheim on Tuesday evening.



3 Kane was quick to ask for assistance in shielding Musiala away from the cameras following his teammate's collapse Credit: Not known, clear with picture desk

But just six minutes after coming off the bench, Musiala collapsed on the pitch for the second time in four days to spark immediate concern.

The ex-Chelsea youth star had previously hit the deck after looking disorientated in Saturday's Telekon Cup encounter with RB Leipzig.

And it was Kane who had picked up on Musiala losing consciousness once again.



In a video shared on social media, the 33-year-old could be seen immediately running towards his stricken teammate as others continued playing.

The former Tottenham striker then proceeded to shield the Germany international in an effort to maintain his privacy.



And he then gestured for more players to come and join him in forming a barrier around the 23-year-old.

What have fans said about Harry Kane's reaction to Jamal Musiala collapsing?

It didn't take long for X users to quickly single out Kane's actions, as one fan said: "King Harold you will always be a king."



Another commented: "A complete and true leader."

A third added: "Kane is class on and off the field."

This supporter then remarked: "That's the spirit of good sportsmanship."

While another simply stated: "Expect nothing less from Harry, classy."

Thankfully, Musiala was able to rise to his feet and walk off the pitch alongside a Bayern physio before being substituted.

While he is expected to rest and recover over the next few days, he is now a doubt to face Borussia Dortmund in Saturday's Beckenbauer Supercup.



Following his latest scare, Musiala released a statement where he declared he has been diagnosed with temporary episodes of absence caused by neurological dysfunction.

What did Jamal Musiala say about his health diagnosis?

Taking to social media, Musiala assured his fans that his condition won't have any lasting effects on his health and career once treated.

He said on Instagram: "First things first - I’m doing well! Above all, I’m incredibly grateful for all your messages and your support.

3 Musiala regained consciousness and was able to walk off the pitch in Heidenheim Credit: Getty



"I understand that many of you are worried. I want to put those concerns to rest today and explain a little more: I have been diagnosed with brief, temporary episodes of absence that are easily treatable and are caused by a neurological dysfunction.

"These can lead to the moments that have occurred recently, such as against Leipzig and now in Heidenheim.

"I know that they may seem scary at first glance - but for me, they are currently simply part of my everyday life.

"I am receiving the best possible medical care in this regard, and I am very optimistic. FC Bayern and the people closest to me are always by my side and supporting me on this journey."



He added: "What is important is that there is no additional health risk beyond this.

"In close consultation and regular communication with the specialists, it was my personal wish to face this challenge and, with the approval of the neurological specialists, to continue doing what helps me most in my recovery: simply living my everyday life and continuing to pursue my passion of playing football.

3 Kane has been praised by fans for his role in protecting Musiala's privacy Credit: Getty

"I have taken responsibility for that decision. Overall, I have a very good feeling and I am on a good path.



"What helps me most along the way is continuing to chase victories and titles with my team, with your incredible support.

"I hope this helps you understand me better.

"At the same time, I ask for your understanding that I would like to continue keeping this matter within the circle of my closest confidants, the club and the experts."

Sports.title: Premier League to hold talks on scrapping 3pm blackout as new streaming era begins
Sports.content:
Premier League to hold talks on scrapping 3pm blackout as new streaming era begins

A decision on ending the 3pm blackout could be made before the end of next season, says Premier League chief executive Richard Masters.

At present, top-flight matches in England cannot be broadcast on live domestic television between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on a Saturday.



3 The 3pm blackout in England could be reviewed within the next two years Credit: Getty

The practice, which is enforced by the FA at the request of the Premier League and EFL, is known as the '3pm blackout'.

When could the 3pm blackout end?

However, it could be removed when the next TV rights cycle is finalised in early 2028.

The current cycle will run through to the end of the 2028/29 season.

As a result, any potential removal of the blackout would not be introduced until the start of the following campaign.



Masters spoke to talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook at the Premier League's season launch on Tuesday - after every Championship match was available for broadcast on Saturday.

Asked if English football is leaning towards the end of the blackout, he explained: "Yes, but it's not just us involved in the decision about Article 48. It's us, the EFL and the FA.



"We've got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change.

"It's not a decision for now. It's a decision we've got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do.



"I'd say in about 18 months' time we'll come back to that decision about whether Article 48 should remain or not."

In-house streaming

The question also comes after the Premier League launched its own streaming service in Singapore.

3 The Premier League are taking its coverage in-house for the first time this upcoming season Credit: Getty

'Premier League +' will show all 380 matches live and provide 24/7 coverage, in what is thought to be a testing ground for possible future streaming in the UK.



talkSPORT's Simon Jordan has long called for the Premier League to launch its own 'Netflix of Football' amid rising subscription costs.

Asked about the new Premier League Studios in west London and its purpose, Masters added: "It gives us stronger options. That's one of the reasons for doing it. Obviously, they're the first job of Premier League Studios.

"It's the size of a football pitch. It's got 29 edit suites. It's got three big studios. It's an impressive facility. It allows us to look at new audiences in a different way.

"But its main job is to provide a world-class production service for our international broadcasters. We're lucky enough to be in growth. This commercial term, which we're now entering the second season of, we've got 27 per cent growth internationally. We've got confidence in the media rights sales model going forward.



"While others are struggling - it's going to be tough in the markets out there - we're back out there doing deals at the moment.

"Within 12 months, we'll be able to announce what the revenue is from 2028-2029 onwards. In Singapore, we've just launched Premier League +, which is our first venture into direct-to-consumer, which is what Simon is talking about, but perhaps on a UK or even global basis.

"We'll learn from that. It's the first time we have our own customers. We've got to manage churn, we've got to set prices.

"We're doing that and we'll learn an enormous amount of it. When you look into the future with Premier League Studios and Premier League +, it does give us greater optionality."



What is the 3pm blackout?

UEFA's Article 48 allows national FAs to nominate a time period when matches cannot be broadcast domestically.

In England, this has been allocated to the 2.45pm to 5.15pm slot on Saturday afternoons ever since the 1960s.

The blackout sees the FA enforce Article 48 at the request of the Premier League and the EFL.

3 Masters has revealed a decision on the 3pm blackout could be made in 18 months' time Credit: Getty



However, there are exceptions allowing for 3pm kick-offs to be broadcast on live TV.

Article 48 can only be enforced when 50 per cent of matches in the top two divisions are being played at the same time within the designated slot.

For the FA to implement the rule, this requires 11 matches across the Premier League and Championship to start at 3pm on a Saturday.

Last weekend's opening round of EFL fixtures saw less than 11 fixtures kick-off at that time in the top two divisions due to the Premier League not starting until this Friday.



As a result, matches in the Championship, League One and League Two could be broadcast domestically.

Although now enforced by UEFA's Article 48, the 3pm blackout has been in place since the 1960s.

It was first introduced to encourage fans to attend lower league matches and boost attendances.

Sports.title: Premier League chief exec admits Man City's 'hugely complex' 115 rule-break charges case is 'taking longer than expected' - leaving fans fuming at new season going ahead with no verdict
Sports.content:
Premier League chief exec admits Man City's 'hugely complex' 115 rule-break charges case is 'taking longer than expected' - leaving fans fuming at new season going ahead with no verdict

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters has admitted it has taken 'longer than expected' for a verdict on their charges against Man City for alleged breaches of financial rules.

Man City, who strongly deny wrongdoing, were charged in February 2023 by the Premier League with a hearing concluding in December 2024.

A three-man panel was tasked with considering the evidence, with the initial expectation a verdict would have been reached on the case within months.

The case now looks set to loom over another season, with the 2026-27 Premier League campaign beginning on Friday.

Speaking to the BBC, Masters described the case as 'hugely complex' as he defended the length of time taken to reach a conclusion.

Masters, however, acknowledged frustration as he admitted the case had taken 'longer than expected.'

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters admitted it has taken 'longer than expected' for a verdict over Man City's alleged breaches of financial rules

The charges relate to alleged breaches which took place at the club between 2009 and 2018

Man City's legal team attend the start of the hearing in September 2024, which concluded in December that year

'As you know I can't really pass any real comment or provide anything new today on it,' Masters said.

'I do accept it is taking longer than expected and I understand that people want to find out as soon as possible what's going on, but I simply can't provide that.

Our rules are very clear, we have to follow the process and there is only one real clear route through, which is to allow that process to reach its natural conclusion.

'I mean it's hugely complex. The hearing took 12 weeks. It has taken longer than expected.'

In a separate interview with Sky Sports, the Premier League chief executive rejected the idea he was 'angry' with the commission over the length of time taken.

'No, I've already said the commission need the time and the space to do their job,' Masters added.

'In the end, the Premier League's role is to put allegations, if the evidence is strong enough, in front of an independent commission and allow that commission to establish the truth, and that shouldn't be qualified by the amount of time it takes to get there.'

The Premier League accused Man City of multiple breaches of financial rules and of failing to co-operate with a subsequent investigation.

Should Man City, who strongly refute any wrongdoing, be found guilty of some of the more serious charges, they could be hit with huge financial penalties, points deductions or even relegation.

Fans on social media appeared frustrated at the lack of updates on the case since the hearing

Man City’s alleged rule breaking is claimed to have taken place over a 14-year period.

The original 115 charges have been extended to a total of 130 after an administration issue.

The club are accused of failing to report accurate financial information for nine seasons stretching from 2009-10 to 2017-18, as well as failing to provide full details of former manager Roberto Mancini’s pay between 2009-10 and 2012-13.

They are also alleged to have failed to provide full details of money paid to players between 2010-11 and 2015-16 and failing to co-operate with the probe from 2018 to 2023.

Fans have reacted with anger at Masters' comments, with the long-running case still yet to be concluded heading into a new season, where Man City will be among the favourites to win the title.

'It's so far beyond a joke now as to make a complete mockery of the whole competition,' one fan wrote.

'Absolute joke - one rule for the likes of City and Chelsea and one rule for everyone else,' a second added.

A third wrote: 'Hearing finished in December 2024... its August 2026.... realistically its never going to conclude is it?

'So same response as about 2 years ago. Absolute farce now by the @premieleague,' added another.

One fan accused the Premier League of attempting to sweep the case under the rug, while others highlighted that other clubs have been charged for financial breaches and verdicts reached within the time the Man City case has been ongoing.

Sports.title: Danny Murphy opens up on losing his cat Bob after viral World Cup commentary - and the surprise reason BBC commentators were forced to MISS matches with illness
Sports.content:
Danny Murphy opens up on losing his cat Bob after viral World Cup commentary - and the surprise reason BBC commentators were forced to MISS matches with illness

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Danny Murphy has opened up on his pet cat Bob - who became an internet sensation during the World Cup - revealing that the whole ordeal was more emotionally turbulent than people realise.

Murphy went viral over the summer when he brought up his missing feline while co-commentating on World Cup matches for the BBC.

Over the course of three tales, he related to the bewildered nation how his former cat, Bob – a beloved British blue shorthair – had gone missing after sneaking inside a Royal Mail van.

They found Bob weeks later, but he returned to the house feral and began fighting with his sister, Mary. Ultimately, Murphy made the heartbreaking decision to rehome Bob with a friend's parents in Preston.

'I used to drive in the area every day for about a month to see if I could see him,' Murphy told Daily Mail Sport.

We're still thinking about Danny Murphy and Bob the Cat.



Commentary camera just dropped. 🫡 pic.twitter.com/pGVRHtz9vJ — Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) July 1, 2026

Danny Murphy has opened up on losing his cat, Bob, in an interview with Daily Mail Sport

Bob, a British blue shorthair, went missing and returned to the house feral, so Murphy had to rehome him

'The guy showed me where he jumped out the van.

'God knows why he jumped in the van! The door was open, maybe he smelled something in there. You never know what's in the back of these Royal Mail vans, do you?

'Then you've got the drama of putting posters out. You'll be amazed at how many people phone you up and lie to you and give you a load of b******* about where the cat is, and they've got the cat, and they want to meet you to get money off you. People don't really understand.

'It was a tough one but because it's a long time ago you get through it and see the funny side.'

Murphy was towards the back end of his career at the time, playing for Tottenham or Fulham, though he can't remember which.

When they did find Bob, it quickly became clear that keeping him alongside his sister Mary was unsustainable – hence why he had to be turfed out.

'He was really feral,' Murphy recalls. 'He had a sister called Mary who lived with us as well, who he decided to attack and bully every day.

'There's no bullying in my household. We had to make the painful decision for him to go.

Murphy recalled losing Bob during a series of World Cup co-commentaries, much to the confusion of the nation

'He ended up having a great life. I sleep easy about it now.'

The 49-year-old has not had a cat since. 'I was always more of a dog man,' he admits.

Murphy was speaking to Daily Mail Sport as he stars in an ad for Paddy Power called 'Why the football not?' celebrating everything ridiculous when it comes to being a football fan.

He began his Match of the Day career in 2013 while he was still a player and has since become a regular broadcast fixture, be that on the iconic show, as a talkSPORT pundit, or a co-commentator.

He took up the mic for 14 matches during the World Cup, an intense period which required extensive preparation. He has since taken the chance to unwind on holiday in Greece.

His ITV counterpart Andros Townsend made waves with his diet during the tournament, tucking into raw meat and sardines to keep himself in the best shape. The temptation on away trips is to fall into a rhythm of gluttonous takeaways and fast food.

Murphy sees where his fellow former England star is coming from.

'I certainly wouldn't be going to Andros' lengths!' he says. 'Even if I did, I certainly wouldn't be telling the world about my eating habits.

@androstownsend Most people don’t fail because they lack information. They fail because the moment life gets inconvenient, their standards disappear. Travel. Hotels. Airports. Busy schedules. That’s usually where good habits go to die. The people who stay healthy long-term aren’t perfect. They just find a way to keep the important things in place, wherever they are. #nutrition #healthyeating #realfood #healthy #wellness ♬ original sound - Andros Townsend

Murphy says he wouldn't follow Andros Townsend's bizarre World Cup diet, but agrees it is important for commentators to stay healthy to perform

'For the first three or four weeks, I was with the commentator Steve Bower. He's quite on the fitness buzz so we were always aware of healthy eating.

'I had good influences. Maybe the odd day we'd let ourselves go and get on the beers and eat a load of c***.

'Doing big games in the World Cup, you're trying to stay focused and peak at the right time. Co-commentary is really intense because you're thinking on your feet - there's no studio where you can plan your analysis.

'The night before a game, when you go to a restaurant in a new city, you have no real idea of where is good or not. You stay plain on the food. You're not just going to go to a Chinese or Indian and say, "fill me up."

'There were a couple of examples of commentators who missed games because of dodgy food. We spoke to another team who were in bed for a week!

'Plain food the night before and decent sleep reflects in your performance. You're not getting names wrong or having blanks. In the football media world, co-comms is the hardest thing to do.'

Sports.title: Aston Villa braced for fourth Ollie Watkins bid from Saudi side, with player open to switch - as Leeds striker Joel Piroe completes West Ham move: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Aston Villa braced for fourth Ollie Watkins bid from Saudi side, with player open to switch - as Leeds striker Joel Piroe completes West Ham move: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa braced for another Watkins bid

Aston Villa anticipate a fourth bid from Al Hilal for striker Ollie Watkins. The England international is open to the move but so far Villa have rejected their advances and want to keep the 30-year-old.

Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins is understood to be open to a move to Saudi Arabia

The latest bid of £38m was rejected on Tuesday evening. Villa maintain interested in Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson and have confirmed the signings of Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Suzuki.

Left back Ruggeri, 24, joins from Atletico Madrid, while goalkeeper Suzuki, 23, arrives after two years in Italy with Parma.

Meanwhile, Rangers have signed right back Kosta Nedeljkovic from Villa.

The 20-year-old has moved to Ibrox on a season-long loan, with a £4m obligation to buy, which will be triggered by the number of games he plays.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed last week, Villa are signing Aaron Wan Bissaka on loan from West Ham pending his medical today.

The deal can become an obligation to buy at around £18million.

Baleba close to United switch

Manchester United are closing on a £65million deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba.

Talks resumed for the Cameroon international in recent weeks after it became apparent his ankle ligament injury was not as serious as first feared.

Read the full story here.

Pogba tears up Monaco deal

Monaco have confirmed that Paul Pogba has left by mutual agreement, bringing his time at the Ligue 1 club to a premature end.

The 33-year-old former Manchester United midfielder is now a free agent and has been offered to clubs in the MLS.

Read the full story here.

James set for Wolves move

Rennes midfielder Jordan James is poised to finalise his move to Wolves today pending his medical.

The Wales international midfielder is joining on an initial loan deal with an option to sign permanently for around £10m.

He impressed on loan at Leicester last season scoring 11 goals in 34 games and had interest from Middlesbrough and West Ham.

Chelsea defender closes on Italy move

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has arrived at Villa Stuart in Rome ahead of his medical this morning.

The 25-year-old centre back is joining Napoli on loan for around £2.5m with an option for the deal to become permanent at £23m.

Mamadou Sarr, meanwhile, is emerging as a target for Real Sociedad and Al Hilal.

The 20-year-old has been expected to go on loan in the Premier League and interest there remains.

The Senegal international was recalled from a loan at Strasbourg to provide cover last season and started in their FA Cup win over Hull.

Piroe party at West Ham

West Ham have signed Joel Piroe on loan from Leeds until the end of the season.

The deal also includes an option for it to become permanent, which will be activated should certain conditions be met, including West Ham winning promotion back to the Premier League.

Joel Piroe has joined West Ham on loan from Leeds

West Ham turned to 27-year-old Piroe after hitting an impasse in talks for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott who is joining Real Betis for £17m plus add ons.

Piroe, who has scored 73 goals in the Championship during spells with Leeds and Swansea , said: 'I see West Ham as a Club that really wants to be in the Premier League, and I think should be in the Premier League.

'With my experience, I think I can help the Club a lot to achieve what they want to achieve, and I think it’s a good opportunity for me to show what I’ve learnt and how I’ve grown as a football player over the years.'

Piroe finished the 2024-25 season as the Championship's top scorer, helping Leeds United earn promotion to the Premier League.

The Hammers remain an option for free agent Jamie Vardy.

Potters snare Ipswich pair

Stoke have agreed a fee of around £6million with Ipswich for striker George Hirst and are also taking Ipswich full back Ben Johnson on loan.

Scotland international Hirst is to undergo medical later today. The fee will increase on performance related bonuses.

Sports.title: Man United close in on £65m deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba
Sports.content:
Man United close in on £65m deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United are closing in on a £65million deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba.

Talks resumed for the 22-year-old Cameroon international in recent weeks after it became clear the ankle ligament injury he suffered during a pre-season friendly against Strasbourg in early August was not as serious as initially feared.

Baleba is expected to return to fitness towards the end of September and is understood to be poised to sign a five-year contract at Old Trafford, keeping him at the club until 2031.

Baleba has been a target for Manchester United for the past year after impressing initially with his industrious performances at Brighton, but he was valued around £75m.

His form dropped away in the second half of last season but United still see enough potential to invest in with his age.

Baleba has also drawn enquiries from Newcastle United in recent weeks.

Talks resumed for the 22-year-old after it became clear the ankle ligament injury he suffered during a pre-season friendly in early August was not as serious as initially feared

With plans to invest in three central midfielders, United have already completed two major signings in Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa (£35m), and Andrey Santo from Chelsea (£50m)

Baleba joined Brighton from Lille for just £23m in 2023 and immediately impressed, establishing himself as one of the most exciting young midfielders in the top-flight.

His dynamism and ability to break the press made him a key figure in Roberto De Zerbi's side before Fabian Hurzeler took charge in 2024.

United looked to sign Baleba last summer, but Brighton wanted in excess of £100m for him and stood firm.

Speaking in October, Brighton's chairman Tony Bloom said: 'There was interest from Manchester United, and we said that he wasn't available this summer and they went away.

'His improvement has been immense. He's a massively important player to this football club, and we're just delighted that he's with us for this season.'

Last season Hurzeler said that the player had struggled with the speculation of a move to United.

'I think it's normal for a young player when the media creates the noise around him,' the young manager said. 'It's not easy for this player to handle it.

'Therefore, we need to give him the time and support so he comes back to his best performance.

'But he's a young player and I think that's something we have to accept, that young players don't always have the face we want to see.'

Prior to Tielemans and Santos' arrival, 21-year-old Kobbie Mainoo was the only established senior central midfielder in the squad

Manuel Ugarte, who United were prepared to offload, sustained a serious knee injury during the World Cup for Uruguay, and will now remain at the club until his expected return in 2027

United set about to reshape their midfield this summer following the departure of the influential Casemiro to MLS side Inter Miami. Manuel Ugarte, who they were prepared to offload, sustained a serious knee injury during the World Cup for Uruguay, will now remain at the club until his expected return at the start of next year.

With plans to invest around £150 million in three central midfielders, they have already completed two major signings in Youri Tielemans, 29, from Aston Villa in a £35m deal, and Andrey Santos, 22, from Chelsea for £50m.

Prior to Tielemans and Santos' arrival, 21-year-old Kobbie Mainoo was the only established senior central midfielder in the squad.

Daily Mail Sport reported in May that United had earmarked around £80 for a marquee signing to replace the Brazilian, and they saw their No 1 target Elliot Anderson head to Manchester City for a record £116m deal. United also agreed terms with Atlanta for Brazil star Ederson but backed out due to concerns over his knee.

Although Michael Carrick has been talking up the importance of giving United's academy players more opportunities, while Tyler Fletcher and Toby Collyer have seen significant game time during pre-season.

Sports.title: Monaco terminate Paul Pogba's contract after ex-Man United star suffered latest injury - only days on from his wife hitting out at claims he should retire
Sports.content:
Monaco terminate Paul Pogba's contract after ex-Man United star suffered latest injury - only days on from his wife hitting out at claims he should retire

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Monaco have terminated Paul Pogba's contract a year early after the French midfielder suffered another setback in his battles with injury.

Pogba had been trying to revive his career following an 18-month doping ban but only featured in six games last season while earning £44,000-a-week at the Ligue 1 side.

The former Man United midfielder suffered a knee issue after 45 minutes of pre-season and another setback with a thigh injury last week.

Monaco have now confirmed an agreement has been reached with Pogba to end his contract early.

The Ligue 1 club praised Pogba's 'unwavering determination' and 'utmost professionalism' during his spell.

'Having jointly concluded that the objectives initially set were only partially achieved, AS Monaco and Paul Pogba have decided, ahead of the first match of the new season, to bring an end to the contract that was due to run until June 2027,' a statement read.

Monaco have confirmed an agreement to end Paul Pogba's contract with immediate effect

Paul Pogba's wife, Zulay (right), defended her husband last week after claims he should retire

'The Club would like to express its heartfelt gratitude to the 2018 FIFA World Cup winner for the trust he placed in the institution and for the utmost professionalism he demonstrated throughout his time in Monaco.

'During his spell in AS Monaco colours, Paul displayed a remarkable mindset, unwavering determination and the highest standards at every moment.

'Through all his efforts, he was able to return to top-level competition after a long period away from the game, while also sharing his experience and expertise with the first-team squad.

'AS Monaco sincerely thanks Paul and wishes him every success in the future.'

Confirmation of Pogba's exit comes days after his wife Zulay, 33, defended her husband online after fans suggested he should consider retirement amid his continued injury problems.

She wrote: 'For all the people saying Paul should retire or he came back to football for the money, let me make this clear, the only one who knows when he will retire is God.

'And for the ones who say he came back for the money, trust me we are very good with money, thank God.'

'Social media accepts everything. People can sit behind a screen and say whatever they want, insult someone, question their intentions and forget that there is an actual human being on the other side.

'For those questioning what he has left to prove, let me remind you he achieved the dream every footballer in the world grows up chasing, dreaming to have. He won the World Cup for his country.'

Zulay is a Bolivian model and influencer and the couple met in 2017 before getting married two years later. They have two sons aged seven and six together.

Daily Mail Sport understands he was offered to MLS clubs last week.

Pogba was cleared to return to football in March 2025 after having a four-year doping ban was reduced to 18 months on appeal.

He had already left Juventus after having that contract terminated by mutual consent in December 2024.

Pogba was emotional when he signed for Monaco last summer, describing his comeback as a second chance after what he called 'a time of darkness'.

The midfielder told Daily Mail Sport in 2024 that he discovered news of his reduced ban while preparing for a film premiere, adding: 'We went through hell. A time of darkness. But this is my second chance, I have to use it.'

Sports.title: Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine as he reveals his secret ban and will 'step away from public life to get myself right'
Sports.content:
Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine as he reveals his secret ban and will 'step away from public life to get myself right'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Nick Kyrgios has revealed that he has failed a drugs test after testing positive for cocaine and received a provisional suspension.

The former Wimbledon finalist has endured a checkered few years after suffering persistent injury, and admitted that the toll they have taken on his career gave 'some context' to his failed test.

'I wanted you to hear it from me first,' Kyrgios began his lengthy statement on Instagram. 'I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine.

'I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it.

'I am sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors, and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself.

'I'm not going to make excuses, but I do want to give some context about where I've been. The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally. My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do, and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.

Nick Kyrgios has shared that he has failed a drugs test after testing positive for cocaine

The former world No13 (pictured in January 2026) has endured a difficult string of seasons amid persistent injury

'I've always said I didn't choose tennis - tennis chose me. But letting go of something that has been my whole life is one of the hardest things I've ever had to face. At times I've felt helpless and alone.

'None of that excuses what I did.

'However, the good news is that this has given me a wake up call. For the next 28 days, I'll be stepping away from social media and public life while I focus on getting myself right.

'I'd ask that people respect my privacy during that time, and most importantly the privacy of my family.

'I'm sorry. I'll do the work and come back better. Nick'.

Kyrgios played in Mallorca at the ATP 250 event in late June, losing his singles match to fellow Australian Adam Walton in straight sets on June 22.

The 31-year-old later withdrew from the doubles, where he and partner John-Patrick Smith had been due to play Austin Krajicek and Nikola Mektic the following day.

Tennis' integrity and anti-doping governing body the ITIA have since announced that Kyrgios has been handed a mandatory provisional suspension.

'The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) has provisionally suspended Australian tennis player Nick Kyrgios under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme,' a statement shared by the organisation read.

'31-year-old Kyrgios provided a sample during an ATP 250 event in Mallorca, Spain, on 22 June 2026. On 17 July 2026, a World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)-accredited laboratory confirmed the presence of benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

'Cocaine is a stimulant and substance of abuse on the WADA Prohibited List and is banned in competition under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme. If taken out of competition, reduced sanctions apply for substances of abuse.

The 31-year-old must now contend with the winding-up of his career, which he has explained has taken a toll on him (pictured in 2022)

'Because of the nature of the substance, a provisional suspension is mandatory and has been in place since 4 August 2026.

'Kyrgios, who reached a career-high world singles ranking of 13 in October 2016, has the right to appeal the provisional suspension, but has not done so to date.

'As with all Tennis Anti-Doping Programme cases, ITIA support is available to Kyrgios.

'While suspended, Kyrgios is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association.'

Before his suspension, Kyrgios' appearances on the tour had been limited, with the combustible Australian star only taking part in a clutch of events due to his prohibitively high ranking of 919.

Offered wildcards to play events in both singles and doubles, the former world No13 has not won a singles match since last year's Miami Open.

Testing positive for cocaine usage could carry a ban from the sport for up to two years, but there is precedence within the sport for a more lenient punishment in light of Kyrgios' admission that he did take the substance. The ban could also be reduced if it was proved that the usage of the drug was not for performance-enhancing benefits.

Former British star Dan Evans was handed a one-year ban in 2017 after testing positive at the Barcelona Open after keeping the drug in the pocket of his washbag.

The International Tennis Federation accepted Evans' explanation that he had become contaminated after the drug found its way onto his finger or medication in the bag accidentally.

Kyrgios' case represents the second high-profile anti-doping revelation in tennis in recent months, after 2023 Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova was handed a four-year ban in June for refusing to take a drugs test.

Sports.title: Dead body found at Charlton Athletic's stadium as club release statement
Sports.content:
A 33-year-old man was found dead at Charlton Athletic's stadium on Tuesday.

Police officers were called to The Valley stadium on Tuesday morning after an incident, which Charlton say occurred on Monday.

The death is being treated as unexpected, with police investigating whether the man fell from a height.

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said: 'At around 11:15hrs on Tuesday, 18 August, officers attended The Valley stadium on Floyd Road, Charlton following concerns for the welfare of a person.

'Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service and located a 33-year-old man, who was sadly pronounced dead at the scene. His next of kin have been informed and continue to be supported.

'Officers are investigating the possibility that the man had fallen from height prior to his death. The death is being treated as unexpected, and an investigation is ongoing.

'Anyone with information is urged to call 101, quoting reference 2809/18AUG.'

The death first came to light in a statement from Charlton on Tuesday evening, which said a body had been discovered at their southeast London stadium.

Charlton said: 'Charlton Athletic are supporting the police with their enquiries following the discovery of a deceased individual at The Valley on Tuesday morning.

'Police were called to the stadium today after an incident that occurred in the early hours of Monday morning. A male was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

'The death remains under investigation. Anyone with information, or who may have witnessed the incident, is asked to contact police on 101, quoting reference 2809/18AUG.'

A dead body was found at The Valley, home of Charlton Athletic, on Tuesday morning

The statement continued: 'Everyone at Charlton Athletic would like to express their deepest sympathies and heartfelt condolences to the individual's family, friends and loved ones at this incredibly difficult time.

'The club are continuing to assist the authorities with their enquiries and respectfully ask that the privacy of those affected is respected. There is no suggestion of any wrongdoing on the part of the club.

'Charlton Athletic would also like to thank its staff for the professionalism they have shown while dealing with a particularly difficult and distressing situation.'

Charlton played at The Valley on Saturday, beating Derby County 2-1 in their first Championship game of the season.

Sports.title: Former Champions League winner, 30, makes shock debut for ninth-tier club - only three months after announcing retirement from football
Sports.content:
Former Borussia Dortmund defender Niklas Sule has returned to football just three months after retiring from the professional game.

Sule, 30, announced that he was bringing his playing career to an end back in May due to a third serious knee injury of his career, having previously ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament twice.

However, he has been surprisingly spotted lacing his boots back up in the ninth tier of German football.

The ex-Germany international made his debut for SV Tiefenbach in the midfield, rather than the centre-back role Dortmund fans were used to seeing him deployed in for four seasons.

Sule, who won the Champions League with Bayern Munich in 2020, marked his first appearance for the club with a goal, towering highest to head into the back of the net.

However, his maiden goal for the club was not enough to prevent them from a 7-2 drubbing at the hands of SG Kirchardt in the opening weekend of their district league.

Niklas Sule has been spotteed playing in the ninth tier of German football despite being retired

The 30-year-old announced his retirement from the professional game back in May

'I think he’s enjoying it more playing a bit more offensively now,' Coach Jason Walzel told Badische Neueste Nachrichten. 'He was there on Saturday and then again on Thursday and Friday.

'I don’t think it was planned that he would one day actually play in the Kreisliga. The boys are happy; he’s a great guy.'

Sule decided his time at the top level was up when he believed he had torn his ACL for the third time in his 13-year professional career.

He went down with what looked like a serious knee problem during Dortmund's 3-2 Bundesliga victory over Heidenheim in February, and following tests with the doctor in the dressing room he 'really thought it's torn'.

However, he escaped another ACL tear and, in that moment, decided that when his Dortmund contract expired, that would be that for his time performing at the highest level.

Speaking to the 'Spielmacher' podcast: 'What I felt when our team doctor did the drawer test [a test used to check for a possible ligament tear] in the dressing room in Hoffenheim, looked at the physio and shook his head, and the physio did it too and didn't feel any resistance either.

'I went into the shower and cried for ten minutes. In that moment, I really thought: "It's torn".

'When I went for an MRI the next day and received the good news [that it wasn't a cruciate ligament tear after all], it was one thousand per cent clear to me that it was over.

Sule marked his return with a debut goal for SV Tiefenbach and played in midfield

Sule (third from left) won the Champions league with Bayern Munich back in 2020

'I couldn't imagine anything worse than looking forward to life - being independent, going on holiday, spending time with my children - only to then have to come to terms with my third cruciate ligament tear.'

Sule started his career at Hoffenheim before moving to Bayern Munich in 2017, where he won five Bundesliga titles in addition to their European triumph over Paris Saint-Germain six years ago.

He made 300 appearances in the Bundesliga, with 78 of those coming in yellow during his four years in Dortmund. Sule was also capped a total of 49 times for his country, scoring once.

Sports.title: Referee chief Howard Webb admits Folarin Balogun red card overturn was 'unhelpful'
Sports.content:
Referee chief Howard Webb admits Folarin Balogun red card overturn was 'unhelpful'

Controversy surrounded the 2026 World Cup this summer after Folarin Balogun was allowed to represent the USA despite being sent off and Howard Webb has now shared his concern

View 2 Images Howard Webb is the head of the PGMOL (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

PGMOL chief Howard Webb has slammed this summer’s controversial Folarin Balogun u-turn at the World Cup as ‘unhelpful’ for referees. The USA striker was sent off in his nation’s last-32 victory against Bosnia & Herzegovina midway and was consequently hit with an automatic ban.

‌



But that decision was reversed following a conversation between FIFA President Gianni Infantino and USA President Donald Trump, allowing Balogun to play in the last-16 clash against Belgium.

‌



That saw the organisation hit with serious criticism, albeit FIFA maintained they did nothing wrong. Former Premier League official and current PGMOL chief Webb has now spoken out and suggested that it might have done more damage for referees.

‌



Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “Integrity in football is so, so important. We live in a world where conspiracy theories are abounding based on nothing, no fact, no evidence.

“Of course, when something like that happens and there’s external pressure applied, it’s not helpful because it creates a space for those conversations to happen.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



“Processes need to be put into place and followed for the integrity of the game. We know suspensions can be appealed in certain competitions and if that process is in place, it’s right that it’s followed.

“Certainly what we saw wasn’t helpful from a refereeing point of view because referees go out there and make a decision based on what they see in moments and that was certainly the case in the Premier League.”

He added: “I don’t think the referee thinks much more about it. They do their job on the day, the VAR does their job on the day.

‌



“I just think that it was the fact that it was admitted post-event that some pressure had been applied and a process implemented. I don’t know the ins and outs of it but at least what we know, it gives fuel to those people that think that those conversations happen all the time and I’m really confident they don’t.

View 2 Images Balogun was sent off against Bosnia but did not have to serve a suspension (Image: Getty Images)

“Anything that gives people energy to fuel conspiracy theories around refereeing decisions is not helpful for us.”

‌



Webb is not the only one to have criticised FIFA for their Balogun u-turn. Premier League chief executive Richard Masters also shared his concern over recent days.

He said: "We worry that about that particular episode, and of course we don't know what happens.

"I don't understand why FIFA doesn't have a very straightforward red card review process in place, like we do in the Premier League, for example. That I think would have would have would have been much a better way to proceed.

Article continues below

"Generally speaking, FIFA is supposed to uphold non-political inference within the game of football. In fact, it's part of its part of its promise that it won't allow it to happen in the rest of the game. So I think it's a big issue, and it needs to be thought through properly."

Sports.title: BBC reveals new Match of the Day line-up with six stars missing and four replacements named
Sports.content:
BBC reveals new Match of the Day line-up with six stars missing and four replacements named

The new Match of the Day line-up for the 2026/27 Premier League has been announced with several familiar names notably missing

Match of the Day: Nedum Onuoha and Stephen Warnock praise Brian Madjo

The BBC has revealed its Match of the Day line-up including four new pundits for 2026/27 Premier League season. But there were six familiar faces - Martin Keown, Dion Dublin, Shay Given, Stephen Warnock, Nedum Onuoha and Theo Walcott - not named in their list of pundits.

‌



Fans will be relieved to hear that top stars Alan Shearer and Wayne Rooney are returning to the show. Joe Hart, Micah Richards, Ellen White, Steph Houghton, Danny Murphy and Ashley Williams will also still be part of MOTD for the new season.

‌



The new quartet joining them are Ashley Young, Robbie Keane, Toby Alderweireld and Thomas Frank, who will all now be part of the revolving door of guests. Mirror Football understands that the omitted names will still play a part in the BBC's football coverage this season.

‌



However, contract negotiations remain ongoing. This announcement comes after The Sun claimed that a number of MOTD pundits were considering leaving to join Gary Lineker's new Netflix show, The Rest Is Football.

Sports.title: New stadium row at heart of Chelsea ownership wrangle as Todd Boehly looks to sell stake
Sports.content:
New stadium row at heart of Chelsea ownership wrangle as Todd Boehly looks to sell stake

Todd Boehly is open to selling his stake in Chelsea just over four years after his arrival at Stamford Bridge and it appears that an argument over the Blues’ stadium is at the centre of his decision

View 2 Images Todd Boehly looks set to sell his stake in Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

A row over the re-development of Stamford Bridge is reportedly at the heart of Todd Boehly’s decision to leave Chelsea. The American arrived in West London back in May 2022 as part of a £4.25bn takeover to replace Roman Abramovich.

‌



Alongside Clearlake Capital, Boehly’s BlueCo consortium have since poured money into the club, with millions having been spent on transfers, as well as managers.

‌



But it appears that Boehly’s time at the helm is set to come to an end, with reports suggesting that he is looking to cash in on his share in the club following disagreements with co-owner Behdad Eghbali.

‌



According to The Sun, a main sticking point is the redevelopment of the Blues’ Stamford Bridge home. Both Boehly and Eghbali agree that Chelsea need a new, purpose-built venue away from the current site but have different visions.

Neither side is willing to provide their share of the £5bn construction cost, while the other camp would still retain huge influence over the project and direction of the West London club.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Boehly is set to leave his role as Chelsea chairman at the end of the season, which could lead to a natural exit, albeit a deal to buy him out is not expected to be easy.

Speaking about the potential of a new stadium in March last year with Bloomberg, Boehly said: “We have a big stadium development opportunity that we have to figure out. And I think the owners will either be aligned, or we ultimately decide to go our different ways.

“It’s not as if we are building something in the middle of a rural environment. We have a lot of constituencies to consider. Certainly, the Chelsea fan base is one. But long-term, I think we’re going to be building something new, and we’ll figure it out.

‌



“Stadium development is happening around the world. You’re going to see the NBA expanding into Europe, new stadiums and arenas being built. We’re just at the very beginning of this wave, and sporting infrastructure will be a major part of it.”

View 2 Images Chelsea have long had plans in place to redevelop Stamford Bridge (Image: Getty Images)

“We’ve been aligned on what we’re trying to do and what we’re trying to build,” he added. “If you look at the evolution of the team, we’ve been working together on building a young squad with long contracts. That was all new. In order to do what we’ve done, it’s because we’re aligned.”

Article continues below

Chelsea had an eye-catching plan for the redevelopment of Stamford Bridge granted planning permission in January 2017, albeit that was scrapped just over a year later, citing an ‘unfavourable investment climate’.

Sports.title: BBC responds to 'mass exodus' fears after Gary Lineker deal and line-up changes
Sports.content:
BBC responds to 'mass exodus' fears after Gary Lineker deal and line-up changes

More pundits could be following Gary Lineker out of the Match of the Day exit door

View 2 Images Mark Chapman, Gabby Logan and Kelly Cates took over as Match of the Day presenters in 2025 (Image: CREDIT LINE:BBC / Charlie Clift)

The BBC is at risk of a mass exodus of pundits with fears growing on the eve of the new Premier League season, it has been claimed. It comes just one year after the broadcaster changed its presenting team for flagship football show Match of the Day, with Kelly Cates, Mark Chapman and Gabby Logan now sharing presenting duties.

‌



Cates, Chapman and Logan took over after Gary Lineker's 25-year stint with the Beeb was brought to an end. Lineker brought his The Rest is Football show to Netflix during the World Cup and has agreed a deal with the streaming service to stay there for the next two Premier League seasons.

‌



According to The Sun, a number of Match of the Day pundits have been weighing up whether to leave for Lineker's new show after Alan Shearer and Micah Richards divided their time between the two during the World Cup. The same publication alleges there have been clashes between BBC head of sport Alex Kay-Jelski and unnamed members of the Match of the Day team.

‌



The same report points to the deal signed between Gary Neville and Disney+ for The Overlap's podcast content, suggesting this too could offer pundits alternatives to Match of the Day. The BBC said in a statement: “We have repeatedly told The Sun these anonymous claims are untrue and we look forward to bringing audiences the return of Match of the Day this weekend with its established line-up of presenters and pundits – alongside a host of new guest voices bringing fresh insight from inside the game.”

While the latest reports point to a fear of further pundit exits, there have also been new additions to the team. Former Tottenham and Belgium defender Toby Alderweireld, who retired from playing in 2025, is among those who will join Match of the Day for the new season.

Lineker had initially been slated to present the BBC's World Cup coverage even after leaving Match of the Day. However this changed when he walked away in May 2025 amid backlash to a social media post and he has since spoken about his life away from the Beeb.

"I've got a bit more time, I'm not treading on quite so many eggshells these days, I'm allowed an opinion on things.," he told the Press Association ahead of the tournament in North America

"But no, I had a wonderful period at the Beeb, and I've covered so many major tournaments, and obviously I was going to do this (the 2026 World Cup) originally, but now I'm doing something different, which is really exciting."

‌



View 2 Images Gary Lineker has been joined by Micah Richards and Alan Shearer on The Rest is Football (Image: Netflix/PA Wire)

At the end of last season, new presenter Cates told Mirror Football about her admiration for the behind-the-scenes team involved in Match of the Day. The presenter has also hosted Sky Sports coverage but appeared positive when discussing her new role.

“Match of the Day is bigger than the presenters,” she said. “I think that's what I've learned, that all the people who work behind the scenes to kind of keep everything on it, they're the people who make the programme what it is.

“Viewers really watch for the football. They're not watching for anything else. I've worked with [the Match of the Day pundits] before. There's nobody who's been brand new to me, that was really nice, but that helps me and it just helps to have some continuity.”

Sports.title: Football fans' biggest gripes revealed - from rising ticket prices to VAR
Sports.content:
Football fans' biggest gripes revealed - from rising ticket prices to VAR

VAR controversies and FIFA's influence are among fan's biggest complaints about the modern game.

View 2 Images Fans are often left frustrated by VAR decisions (Image: Getty Images)

Football fans' biggest gripes include FIFA, soaring ticket prices and Super Bowl-style half-time shows. Research of 5,000 fans found 61% believe the sport has lost its way. The study revealed much of fans' frustrations stemmed from spiralling costs, with 88% feeling like ordinary supporters are being priced out.

‌



Alongside ticket prices, this included the number of subscriptions needed to watch games, as well as the Champions League not being free-to-air. But that wasn't all. Many also complained about the number of kits released by teams each season, while others dislike colourful football boots.

‌



The research was commissioned by OLBG to celebrate the launch of the Marc White Fixes Football show. The Dorking Wanderers founder and manager, said: "The feeling that fans are being priced out of football really stands out from the study.

‌



"Following your club has become more expensive than ever, and supporters are noticing it. Football doesn't exist without fans, so it's important the game doesn't lose sight of that. "

View 2 Images Supporters feel the game has lost what made it special (Image: Getty Images)

When asked what they would do if they were in charge of the game, many said they would enforce cheaper tickets. The next biggest priorities were scrapping VAR, making more matches free-to-air and reducing the influence bodies like FIFA have on the sport.

‌



When it comes to VAR, just 18% said they would keep it as it is, with the biggest issues being the time it takes, the game feeling too stop-start and it creating more debate than it solves.

If participants were to make changes, they would introduce greater consistency, quicker decisions and even a time limit for reviews.

Respondents were also unhappy with half-time shows. Only a quarter said they enjoyed this year's World Cup Final performance.

‌



Nearly three quarters (72%) felt negatively about the idea of bringing in such shows on a more regular basis, while 31% branded it "a terrible idea".

White added: "Fans are the lifeblood of the game, but a lot of them feel football is drifting further away from the people who made it what it is.

"People still love football, they just want decisions to be made with supporters at the heart of them."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola transfer risk as Rio Ngumoha switch could be forced
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola transfer risk as Rio Ngumoha switch could be forced

Liverpool continue to be linked with the signing of PSG winger Bradley Barcola

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola still has plenty of work to do before the transfer window closes (Image: Darren Staples / AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool could opt for a riskier approach in their attempts to sign Bradley Barcola this summer. The Paris Saint-Germain winger is the Reds' number one target, but a deal to clinch his signature has yet to be completed.

‌



Andoni Iraola has overseen a somewhat quiet transfer window in his opening months as Liverpool boss, having only brought in Victor Munoz and Ronald Araujo. The Spaniard will be hoping he can seal further arrivals before the window slams shut on September 1.

‌



Iraola is also deep in preparation for the Reds' Premier League season-opener on Sunday away to Newcastle United. Amid the reported riskiness that Liverpool could utilise in their chase of Barcola, Rio Ngumoha is already primed for a major switch this season.

‌



Barcola risk

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola remains a target for Liverpool this summer (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

The fee for Barcola remains to be the sticking point between PSG and Liverpool, it has been claimed. The French champions had reportedly valued the 23-year-old at £145million, with the Reds unwilling to do a deal at that price.

This has led to Liverpool playing something of a waiting game, in the hope PSG's own transfer business helps lower the price for the Frenchman. The Ligue 1 champions have subsequently sealed the arrivals of Maghnes Akliouche, Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, softening their stance on keeping hold of Barcola.

‌



Liverpool reach agreement with PSG star as attacking double deal takes shape READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

French outlet Jeunes Footeux [via Liverpool.com] reports PSG have now reduced their asking price for Barcola, vindicating the Reds' risky transfer tactic. But journalist Ben Jacobs has said on talkSPORT [via This Is Anfield] that the Premier League giants could take a risk if they continue to try and wait out the possible deal until the final days of the window to force PSG to lower their asking price further.

Ngumoha switch

View 3 Images Rio Ngumoha could play at right-wing this season (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

‌



Barcola's possible arrival will see the France international play in his favoured left-wing position, which would cause Nguomha to earn most of his game time on the right flank, according to The Times. The Reds have yet to replace Mohamed Salah this summer, but it is claimed the 17-year-old is the likely candidate to succeed the Egyptian.

Ngumoha has featured on the right wing a considerable amount during pre-season and started in the role in the club's final friendly against Como on Sunday. Versatility from wingers is something Iraola requires and previously had at Bournemouth, with the likes of Antoine Semenyo and Dango Ouattara often deployed in different roles.

Sports.title: Arsenal chief makes transfer window vow as Mikel Arteta shortlist revealed
Sports.content:
Arsenal chief makes transfer window vow as Mikel Arteta shortlist revealed

Arsenal have so far spent heavily by signing Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincapie as they attempt to defend their Premier League title with more business potentially on the horizon

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has spoken out on Arsenal's summer business (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal chief executive Richard Garlick has vowed that the Premier League champions are still open to more signings this summer - but only if they move the Gunners forward.

‌



Mikel Arteta’s side have already spent heavily this summer in their attempts to retain the Premier League title. Defender Piero Hincapie has signed a permanent deal, while Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes have arrived for a combined £110m.

‌



They have continued to be linked with other switches including for Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez - albeit they now appear to be unlikely.

‌



CEO Garlick has now spoken out on his side’s potential business and has not ruled out more incomings but only if a certain player takes the club to the next level.

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: "It's players that are going to take Arsenal forward. In the past we've looked at players that maybe helped build out the squad or get us to a certain level, but now we're competing right at the top level, and we do need to bring in players that are going to change the dial.

‌



"That might be younger players that come into your squad and give them time to develop, and you've seen that in the last couple of years at Arsenal, and if we're able to combine those players that are coming through the academy with some of the best players in the world then we've got every chance of maintaining that success and going beyond what we've already achieved."

He added: "We said at the start of this season we're about to embark on that we're not going to stand still and pat ourselves on the back and say, 'Well done, job done, nothing else to do'. We want to move forward - the best clubs are always moving forward.

"You can see we've already invested in the squad this season, and if the right opportunity arises, then we will look to strengthen in all areas.

‌



"The window's open for the next couple of weeks, and if there are players that are going to come in and move Arsenal forward, then we will look at that.

View 2 Images Arsenal have already signed Bruno Guimaraes (Image: Getty Images)

"The standard now is high, though - the bar's been set winning the Premier League title and getting to the Champions League final. We're probably fishing in a smaller pool of quality players, and that means that it's tricky to land those players that are going to drive Arsenal forward. But if the right opportunity presents itself, we'll certainly be exploring it."

‌



Garlick’s comments are similar to ones from Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, who has suggested that he will only want players who progress the squad.

He said: "It's certainly the ambition of the club and the owners to be the best club in the world. In order to do that, you need the best facilities, the best stadium, the best supporters, and you need the best squad and the best players in the world.

"Those are the ones that win you football matches and the ones that can be decisive when it matters. That's what we try to build with the actual players that we have, and with the players that we want to sign to make the difference for Arsenal."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
